To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LIF and Interleukins 6 (IL- 6) are up regulated in the sciatic nerve and in the denervate muscle following transection.

1) both LIF and IL6 mRNAs were up-regulated in injured sciatic nerve, with proximal and distal segments showing similar levels of mRNA; 2) LIF, but not IL6, was retrogradely transported in the sciatic nerve; 3) LIF, not IL6, stimulated survival of sensory neurons, in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of growth factors in the peripheral nervous system.
the role of LIF in peripheral nerve injury and regeneration, and the possible role of LIF as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of peripheral nerve injury.
the study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the regeneration of peripheral nerves after injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LIF is a trauma factor, whereas IL-6 may be a neurotrophic factor for the central nervous system.
LIF is a neurotrophic factor, whereas IL-6 is a trauma factor.

LIF and interleukin (IL)6 expression are up-regulated in the sciatic nerve and denervated skeletal muscle after injury, that LIF and Schwann cells and muscle cells are the main source of the cytokines, and that LIF but not IL-6 is retrogradely transported by the sciatic axon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LIF is retrogradely transported and is neurotrophic to sensory neurons, and IL-6 is produced by Schwann cell, but is not retrogradly transported, and is not neurotrophic to motor or sensory neurons.
the up-regulation of IL-6 in the nerve segments and muscle after nerve injury, may play a role in the inflammatory process and in the regeneration of the injured nerve.
the LIF and IL6 are up-regulated after injury, and LIF acts on sensory neurons, and IL6 on Schwann cells, but not on neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LIF/STAT3 pathway plays an important role in the development of peripheral nerve regeneration.
LIF and its related cytokine IL-6 are upregulated after peripheral nerve injury.
LIF and its receptor are expressed in injured nerve and muscle.
